Jeremiah confesses on behalf of the people that their fathers sinned by worshiping idols and evil lusts, and the discipline of the Lord came upon the sons, because they walked in the way of their fathers' sins, so they deserved punishment.

Do not give up your spiritual weapons and your food, which are Holy Communion, the word of God and prayer, lest Satan deprive you of them and you obtain them with difficulty afterward. Hold fast to your spiritual rule and compel yourself to it, for what you compel yourself to today you will become accustomed to and enjoy tomorrow.
[2] Humiliation (vv. 8-18)

8- Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand. 9- We gat our bread with the peril of our lives because of the sword of the wilderness. 10- Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine. 11- They ravished the women in Zion, and the maids in the cities of Judah. 12- Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders were not honoured. 13- They took the young men to grind, and the children fell under the wood. 14- The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their musick. 15- The joy of our heart is ceased; our dance is turned into mourning. 16- The crown is fallen from our head: woe unto us, that we have sinned! 17- For this our heart is faint; for these things our eyes are dim. 18- Because of the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, the foxes walk upon it.

Jerusalem was a great city, and the people of God took pride in the presence of the temple in their midst, and they were exalted above all the peoples by their knowledge of God, but when they forsook God they grew weak, and those weaker than they, who were spiritually like slaves to them, gained dominion over them, so they became their chiefs and occupiers, and their occupation lasted long and none of the surrounding peoples delivered them, because God wanted to discipline them for 70 years, which is the duration of their captivity.

Because of the cruelty of the Babylonian occupation that controlled the streets of Jerusalem and the land of Judea, it became hard for the people of God to obtain their bread, that is, the necessary sustenance, so they used to seize the opportunity to gather some grains of wheat or barley or fruits of the field to satisfy their hunger.

Oven: a furnace. The hunger grew severe upon the people of God and lasted long, so their skin clung to their bones and even became dark, tending to black, as though their skins had been burned in an oven and become black.
The hand of the soldiers of Babylon reached out to assault and rape the virgin women of the people of God. So Satan humiliates the one who submits to him through evil lusts.
The Babylonian humiliation extended and tortured the people, especially their chiefs, whom they hanged up by their hands in the air, and the hand of torture reached the elders as well as the young.

Be careful of sin, whether you are a man or a woman, a young man or a young woman or in old age, for Satan exploits every opportunity to make you fall into sin. So guard against the sources of sin and keep away from them, and if you fall, repent quickly so that God may raise you up and you may trample the devil.

Babylon used the young men of the people of God for grinding, exploiting their strength instead of the women who used to grind at the mill, and as for the boys, they exploited them to work in the houses carrying wood and lighting fires, so they fell from intense exhaustion.

The elders were accustomed to sit at the gate of the city for judging and settling disputes, but after the ruin of the land they no longer sat in the square at the gate, and on the other hand the young men were in sorrow and no longer sang songs of joy. When a person is lax toward sin he loses his ability to discern and judge, and he also loses his joy.
Joy departed from the hearts of the people of God, and instead of expressing joy with dancing games they were weeping over the humiliation in which they found themselves.
Their glory was also lost, which is expressed by the crown they wear on their heads. All this is discipline from God because of our sins.
Hearts became sorrowful and eyes grew weak from much weeping, and this symbolizes the weakness of spiritual insight in sinners and their loss of peace and happiness
Jerusalem, built on five mountains, the most important of which is Mount Zion, became a ruin, and instead of her sons walking on these mountains she became deserted of people and foxes run in her.

19- Thou, O LORD, remainest for ever; thy throne from generation to generation. 20- Wherefore dost thou forget us for ever, and forsake us so long time? 21- Turn thou us unto thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old. 22- Hast thou utterly rejected us? art thou very wroth against us?

The hearts of the people of God turn to Him in hope that He may deliver them from their humiliation, and they declare their faith in His power, for He is the King of kings who sits on His throne in heaven and His kingdom is perpetual forever, whereas all the peoples of the world are passing away and their power is temporary; rather, He uses them to carry out His will.

The people of God entreat Him not to leave them long under this discipline and humiliation under the hand of Babylon, and from the length of the period and the severity of the discipline they felt that it was a long time, so they entreated God to remove the punishment from them.

In hope the people ask God to bring them back to Him and renew their life in Him, so they return and worship Him in purity, for their return from captivity is a return to the worship of God in His temple, that is, it is a spiritual return and not a return to possessing lands and material good things.
The people of God ask from the depth of tribulation, and protest to God that He should reject them utterly and be angry with them forever, because He is their merciful and tender Father.

Entreat God in all your needs and trust that He loves you and wants to remove every tribulation from you, but He waits for your faith and your love for Him, which appears in the persistence of prayer.
The life of Jeremiah

1- Jeremiah is a Hebrew word meaning "God establishes" or "God repairs," and the name of the prophet indicates the purpose of his ministry, for he will root out, pull down, build and plant (Jer 1:10).

2- Jeremiah was born in the village of Anathoth, which lies northeast of Jerusalem at a distance of three miles, and it is a village set apart for the dwelling of priests (Josh 21:18). Jeremiah was of priestly descent, and his great forefather was Abiathar, who was high priest with Zadok in the days of David the prophet. Jeremiah was a priest and a prophet, but he focused his ministry on prophecy and not on the priesthood.

3- Jeremiah was born in 646 BC at the end of the reign of Manasseh king of Judah, and in his childhood and youth he was a contemporary of Josiah, the righteous king. Because Josiah did not begin his reforms until eighteen years after he became king, Jeremiah saw corruption surrounding him on every side, which troubled him greatly, since he loved God.
4- Jeremiah was influenced by the prophets before him, who confronted corruption with strong prophecies, such as Isaiah, Zephaniah, Hosea and Obadiah.

5- Jeremiah was tender in feeling and a lover of God, so he felt God's distress and wrath at the evils of his people. God called him while he was a young man to proclaim His prophecies, and he began his prophecies when he was twenty years old, and that was in the thirteenth year of Josiah, that is, in 626 BC. Josiah had not yet begun his religious reforms. Thus Jeremiah, by his prophecies, was an encouragement to Josiah to begin his reforms by destroying the idols and restoring prayer to the temple of God.

6- When God called Jeremiah to the ministry of prophecy, he excused himself and pleaded that he was young and unable to perform this ministry, but God encouraged him, so he rose and began his ministry (Jer 1:5-7).
7- Jeremiah prophesied, and rebuked all classes of the people for their sins: the king, the chiefs, the teachers, the prophets, the scribes and the people at large, that they might repent.

8- Jeremiah loved virginity, then God commanded him to it so that he might be an illustrative image for the people, because there would be no stability, since captivity was coming, and therefore there was no opportunity for marriage and begetting children (Jer 16:2). All this was so that they might turn back from the worship of idols and their evil lust.
The life of Jeremiah

9- After Jeremiah had gone on with his prophecies, and Josiah with his reforms, Hilkiah the high priest found a copy of the Law in the temple, and when Josiah read it he was deeply moved and tore his clothes, and Josiah consulted Huldah the prophetess, who declared God's wrath upon the people and that He would punish them with captivity, but because of Josiah's humbling himself this would come after his death. So the prophecies of Huldah confirmed the prophecies of Jeremiah, which encouraged Jeremiah to continue his rebuke and his call of his people to repentance (2 Chr 34:22).

10- King Josiah kept the Passover, and called to it not only the inhabitants of his kingdom Judah but also those remaining of the twelve tribes, who had been taken captive by the kingdom of Assyria, and Jeremiah rejoiced at the people's return to God at this great celebration.

11- Jeremiah continued his rebuke of the people, but they rejected his prophecies, relying on the beginning of the decline and weakness of the kingdom of Assyria, which ruled the world and enslaved them. They saw that there was no danger to them, so they did not fear or obey God through the mouth of Jeremiah, and did not believe that their city would be ruined, and likewise their temple, forgetting that God is able to permit its destruction at the hand of any man, as happened at the hand of Babylon.

12- When Jeremiah reached the age of thirty-seven, Necho king of Egypt killed King Josiah (2 Chr 35:20-24), and his son Jehoahaz became king. He was weak and young, and sadly he restored the worship of idols. So Necho king of Egypt took him captive, and made Jehoiakim his brother king in his place. Jehoiakim was also wicked, and continued in idol worship. All this troubled Jeremiah, but he continued his prophecies and his call of the people to repentance.

13- Jeremiah warned King Jehoiakim to repent and walk like his father Josiah, but he did not obey him. And Jeremiah proclaimed his prophecies at the gate of the house of the Lord to all the people, that God was calling them to repentance and that captivity was coming upon them. But the people did not repent, and the false prophets deceived them (Jer 20:1, 2) that they would have peace, and the priests helped them in this evil.

14- They seized Jeremiah and imprisoned him, and Jeremiah thought of not continuing his prophecies, but the word of God was like fire within him, so he returned to prophesy, and God supported him and strengthened him (Jer 20:7-9). The life of Jeremiah

15- The priests prevented Jeremiah from entering the temple, so he dictated his prophecies to Baruch the prophet, who read them at the gate of the house of the Lord and to the chiefs. And they informed the king, who was angry and burned the prophecies (Jer 36:20-26), so Jeremiah dictated them a second time, and Baruch wrote them, and after this Jeremiah and Baruch remained in hiding, because the king wanted to kill them (Jer 22:19).

16- King Jehoiakim died and his corpse was cast on the ground like a donkey, as Jeremiah prophesied (Jer 22:19). And his son Jehoiachin reigned for three months, then the king of Babylon took him captive and made his uncle Zedekiah king in his place (2 Chr 36:9, 10). He was weak in character, at times showing submission to Jeremiah, then turning against him after this through submission to the wicked chiefs of Judah. Jeremiah had reached the age of 48 when Zedekiah became king.
17- After four years of Zedekiah's reign he rebelled against the king of Babylon, so the king of Babylon summoned him and rebuked him, and he was very afraid.

18- The wicked chiefs of Judah rose against Jeremiah and imprisoned him in a harsh prison, and some time after this Zedekiah moved him to a less harsh prison, as he wanted to hear some counsels from him (Jer 37:18-21). And after Jeremiah was brought out he was imprisoned again in a harsh prison, and one of the few pious chiefs interceded, so they brought him out (Jer 38:7-12). Jeremiah bore all this with wonderful patience, but continued in courage to proclaim the prophecies of God that the Babylonian captivity was coming upon them and that they must repent.

19- Jeremiah was a contemporary of other prophets who prophesied the word of God and called the people to repentance, such as Habakkuk the prophet and Urijah the prophet, who prophesied in the land of Judah, which encouraged Jeremiah, and likewise Ezekiel the prophet prophesied in Babylon with prophecies that confirm the prophecies of Jeremiah; all these prophecies were warnings from God that the people might repent.

20- The king of Babylon besieged Jerusalem several times after attacking the land of Judea, and in the end Jerusalem fell into the hand of Babylon, and he burned her and her temple (Jer 34), and that was in 587 BC. Jeremiah's age at that time was 59, and Zedekiah fled, but the men of Babylon seized him and his sons and killed them The life of Jeremiah Nebuchadnezzar before his eyes, then put out Zedekiah's eyes and sent him to Babylon to be imprisoned there (2 Kgs 25:4-6).

21- Jeremiah remained in Jerusalem and was like a tender father weeping over his people, and he wrote the Book of Lamentations known by his name. And he called the people to repentance and submission to Babylon and not to seek shelter in Egypt, but they did not obey him and went to Egypt, and even carried him against his will to Egypt.

22- Jeremiah continued to call his people in Egypt to repent and not to worship the idols of Egypt and to submit to Babylon, which would attack Egypt, so the Jews were troubled by him and rose against him and stoned him, and he was martyred in Egypt after reaching the age of 60, having prophesied to his people for more than 40 years.

23- Jeremiah was a symbol of Christ, who came to His own and His own received Him not (Jn 1:11), and he bore sufferings to death, like Christ, so he died at the hand of his people whom he had shepherded throughout his life.
